title: Max Points on a Line
prompt: Given an array of `points` where `points[i] = [xi, yi]` represents a point on the X-Y plane, return the maximum number of points that lie on the same straight line.

examples.explanation: All three points lie on the line y = x.
With only a single point, it trivially lies on infinitely many lines by itself, so the answer is 1.

hints: Checking every triple of points for collinearity is O(n^3). Fixing just one point at a time and comparing slopes to it is enough.
For a fixed anchor point, group every other point by the slope of the line it forms with the anchor — points sharing a slope relative to the same anchor are collinear with it.

Represent slope as a reduced fraction (dy/gcd, dx/gcd) with a consistent sign convention instead of a floating-point division, to avoid precision errors, and handle vertical lines (dx == 0) as a special slope key.

solution.approach: For each point used as an anchor, compute the slope from that anchor to every other point, and count how many points share each slope using a hash map — all points sharing a slope relative to the same anchor lie on the same line through it. To avoid floating-point precision issues, represent a slope as a reduced (dy, dx) pair using their GCD, with a fixed sign convention so that opposite-direction pairs normalize to the same key (and a dedicated key for vertical lines where dx = 0). The best count found across all anchors, plus the anchor point itself, is the answer. This reduces the search to O(n^2) instead of checking all O(n^3) triples.
